key_insight: A unified crystal plasticity-fracture model shows that creep cracking shifts from transgranular at high stress to mixed and then intergranular at lower stress, driven by the competition between slip-induced intragranular cracking and grain-boundary cavitation.
engineering_relevance: This clarifies how stress level controls rupture mode, ductility, and lifetime in high-temperature metals, helping guide alloy design and service-life prediction.
method: Coupled crystal plasticity with grain-boundary cavitation
Crystallographic crack propagation to capture inter- and trans-granular transition
evidence_signal: Microscale simulations reproduce a stress-dependent transition in crack morphology and damage localization, linking these patterns to changes in rupture ductility and creep life.
watch_item: The framework is computationally detailed, so calibration and computational cost may limit direct use without material-specific parameters and efficient implementation.
paper_title: Mechanistic transition between inter- and trans-granular creep cracking via a unified crystal plasticity-fracture framework
